accepted.s: In the capability approach to development, the ultimate criteria of development are:
accepted.x: The capability approach treats people and their capabilities, rather than economic growth alone, as the ultimate criteria of development.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that expresses the underlying human-centred concept rather than a narrow economic indicator.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who is associated with the capability approach that defines development as the expansion of freedoms?
accepted.x: Amartya Sen's capability approach views development as the expansion of real freedoms.
accepted.tq: Use the person-concept association to distinguish the principal theorist from related contributors.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the capability approach:
1. Development is viewed as the expansion of real freedoms.
2. Martha Nussbaum extended the approach by presenting a list of central human capabilities.
3. The approach treats income as the final objective of development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because income is a means to development, not its ultimate end.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the means-and-end distinction in human development.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following illustrates the role of policy choices in determining human development outcomes?
o: HDI is determined exclusively by GNI per capita
Malaysia has higher GNI per capita than Chile, but Chile has a higher HDI
Chile has higher GNI per capita and lower HDI than Malaysia
Both countries have identical life expectancy and schooling outcomes
accepted.x: Malaysia has higher GNI per capita, but Chile has a much higher HDI because of better life expectancy and schooling outcomes.
accepted.tq: Compare the income ranking with the HDI ranking instead of assuming that income alone determines development.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Compared with Malaysia, Chile has approximately:
o: The same life expectancy but 3 more years of expected schooling
7 fewer years of life expectancy and 3 fewer years of expected schooling
7 more years of life expectancy and 3 more years of expected schooling
3 more years of life expectancy and 7 more years of expected schooling
accepted.x: Chile has approximately seven more years of life expectancy and three more years of expected schooling than Malaysia.
accepted.tq: Separate the two numerical comparisons and match each figure with the correct indicator.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding income and HDI?
o: GNI is a means of development, whereas HDI captures broader human development outcomes
GNI can completely replace HDI because income is the end of development
HDI ignores all non-income dimensions of development
Countries with higher GNI per capita must always have higher HDI
accepted.x: Income is a means rather than the end of development, and HDI incorporates health and education along with income.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute claims and select the option that preserves the distinction between income and human outcomes.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Kerala Model of development?
o: Low human development caused exclusively by low literacy
High human development associated with modest income
High income accompanied by the lowest human development
Rapid industrialisation without improvement in social indicators
accepted.x: The Kerala Model is characterised by high human development despite comparatively modest income.
accepted.tq: Match the model with its distinctive development pattern rather than with a single income measure.
accepted.sec: Human development concept - capabilities; same GNI, different HDI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of the HDI methodology, the dimension index is calculated as:
o: (Actual value − Minimum value) ÷ (Maximum value − Minimum value)
accepted.x: The dimension index equals (actual value minus minimum value) divided by the difference between the maximum and minimum values.
accepted.tq: Recall the normalisation formula by identifying the subtraction of the minimum from the actual value.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding HDI goalposts:

List-I (Indicator)
a. Life expectancy
b. Expected years of schooling
c. Mean years of schooling
d. GNI per capita

List-II (Minimum–Maximum)
i. 0–18 years
ii. 100–75,000 PPP dollars
iii. 20–85 years
iv. 0–15 years

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The goalposts are 20–85 years for life expectancy, 0–18 for expected schooling, 0–15 for mean schooling and 100–75,000 PPP dollars for GNI per capita.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive GNI range and then eliminate codes using the schooling ranges.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s: The education index in the HDI is obtained by taking the:
o: Geometric mean of life expectancy and income indices
Simple ratio of expected years to mean years of schooling
Arithmetic mean of the expected-years and mean-years schooling sub-indices
Weighted mean of GNI and schooling indices
accepted.x: The education index is the arithmetic mean of the indices for expected years of schooling and mean years of schooling.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific aggregation method used within the education dimension.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s: Why is the logarithm of GNI per capita used in calculating the income index of the HDI?
o: To convert GNI into life expectancy
To give income a zero weight
To reflect diminishing returns to income
accepted.x: The logarithm captures diminishing returns: an additional unit of income contributes less to human development at higher income levels.
accepted.tq: Link the mathematical transformation with its economic rationale rather than treating it as a unit conversion.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the HDI:
1. It is the geometric mean of the three dimension indices.
2. The geometric-mean method was introduced in 2010.
3. Under this method, a strong dimension can fully offset a weak dimension.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the geometric mean prevents a strong dimension from fully offsetting a weak one.
accepted.tq: Test the effect of geometric aggregation by rejecting the reversed implication about offsetting weaknesses.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s: The use of PPP dollars in HDI income comparisons primarily enables comparison across:
accepted.x: Purchasing Power Parity dollars allow income to be compared fairly across countries with different price levels.
accepted.tq: Match the statistical adjustment with the cross-country problem it is designed to address.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s: The HDI value of Georgia mentioned in the methodology example is approximately:
accepted.x: The worked example gives Georgia an HDI value of approximately 0.769, classified as high human development.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive decimal value rather than confusing it with nearby HDI scores.
accepted.sec: Methodology - dimension indices, goalposts, geometric mean, GNI PPP

accepted.s: According to the Human Development Report 2023–24, based on HDI values for 2022, India was ranked:
accepted.x: India was ranked 134th among 193 countries in the HDR 2023–24, based on HDI values for 2022.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the report edition, reference year and total number of countries before selecting the rank.
accepted.sec: Human Development Report - India's rank and top-ranked country  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The same simulation estimated that India's poverty rate could rise from 23.9 per cent to:
accepted.x: The estimated poverty rate rises from 23.9 per cent to 24.2 per cent, implying about 24.6 lakh additional poor people.
accepted.tq: Compare the exact starting and projected percentages rather than choosing the nearest rounded figure.
accepted.sec: Human Development Report - India's rank and top-ranked country  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Global and National MPI:
1. Both use the Alkire–Foster method.
2. Both have health, education and standard of living as their three dimensions.
3. The National MPI has 12 indicators, whereas the Global MPI has 10 indicators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The National MPI retains the three equally weighted dimensions, uses the Alkire–Foster method and expands the indicator count to 12.
accepted.tq: Use the common features first, then verify the numerical distinction in the indicator counts.
accepted.sec: MPI - global (UNDP-OPHI) vs national (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which two indicators are added in India's National MPI to the Global MPI framework?
accepted.x: India's National MPI adds maternal health and bank account indicators, making the framework SDG-aligned with 12 indicators.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between indicators specifically added to the national framework and plausible but unsupported additions.
accepted.sec: MPI - global (UNDP-OPHI) vs national (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the standard of living dimension of the MPI?
accepted.x: Expected years of schooling belongs to the education dimension. Cooking fuel, sanitation and drinking water are standard-of-living indicators.
accepted.tq: Classify each option by dimension and find the education indicator in a living-standard list.
accepted.sec: MPI - global (UNDP-OPHI) vs national (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the National MPI based on NFHS-5 data for 2019–21, the MPI value for India was:
accepted.x: The National MPI value based on NFHS-5 for 2019–21 was 0.066; its headcount ratio was 14.96 per cent and intensity was 44.39 per cent.
accepted.tq: Separate the national MPI value from the different global MPI values reported for other years.
accepted.sec: MPI - global (UNDP-OPHI) vs national (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National MPI is monitored under which initiative?
o: Inclusive Development and Human Capital Initiative
Global Indices for Reforms and Growth
accepted.x: The National MPI is monitored under the Global Indices for Reforms and Growth initiative.
accepted.tq: Match the index-monitoring arrangement with its exact official initiative name.
accepted.sec: MPI - global (UNDP-OPHI) vs national (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches an instrument of inclusive growth with its principal contribution?
o: Self-Help Groups — women's credit and livelihood support
Financial inclusion — exclusion of small borrowers from formal finance
DBT — replacement of welfare transfers by export subsidies
accepted.x: Self-Help Groups support women's credit and livelihoods. MSMEs are associated with labour-intensive jobs, while financial inclusion and DBT broaden access and delivery.
accepted.tq: Match each instrument with its stated inclusive-growth function and reject reversed effects.
accepted.sec: Inclusive growth - pillars, Eleventh Plan, instruments  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MSMEs can promote inclusive growth through labour-intensive employment.
2. Welfare-oriented DBT is an instrument of inclusive growth.
3. SHGs are associated with women's credit and livelihood opportunities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. MSMEs, DBT and SHGs are identified as instruments that can widen participation in growth.
accepted.tq: Recognise several complementary instruments rather than treating inclusive growth as a single-sector policy.
accepted.sec: Inclusive growth - pillars, Eleventh Plan, instruments  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: India's Gini coefficient declined from 36.8 in 2004–05 to which value in 2019–20?
accepted.x: The Gini coefficient fell from 36.8 in 2004–05 to 32.1 in 2019–20.
accepted.tq: Use the paired years to distinguish the later value from nearby plausible inequality figures.
accepted.sec: Inclusive growth - pillars, Eleventh Plan, instruments  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match the following indices with the year of their introduction in Human Development Reports:

a. Capability Poverty Measure
a. Human Poverty Index
c. Gender Development Index
d. Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI

i. 1995
ii. 1996
iii. 1997
iv. 2020

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: CPM was introduced in 1996, HPI in 1997, GDI in 1995 and PHDI in 2020.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive 2020 PHDI pair and then place the three earlier indices chronologically.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Capability Poverty Measure primarily measures:
accepted.x: The Capability Poverty Measure, introduced in 1996, measures deprivation in basic capabilities.
accepted.tq: Match the index with its stated subject matter rather than with another poverty or gender index.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement about the Human Poverty Index is correct?
o: HPI-1 applied to developing countries and HPI-2 to developed countries
HPI was introduced in 1995 and measures only income poverty
HPI measures only gender disparities in HDI
accepted.x: HPI-1 was designed for developing countries and HPI-2 for developed countries. The HPI was later replaced by MPI in 2010.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two HPI variants by country group and avoid reversing the replacement sequence.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Gender Development Index?
o: Ratio of female HDI to male HDI
HDI adjusted only for carbon emissions
accepted.x: The GDI is the ratio of female to male HDI, covering health, education and earned income.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerator–denominator relationship to distinguish GDI from GII.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index:
1. IHDI was introduced in 2010.
2. It discounts HDI for inequality.
3. IHDI is lower than HDI whenever inequality exists.
4. The difference between HDI and IHDI represents the loss due to inequality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. IHDI adjusts potential human development for inequality and the gap from HDI indicates the loss due to inequality.
accepted.tq: Check each defining property of the index, including the interpretation of the HDI–IHDI gap.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Gender Inequality Index covers which of the following areas?
o: Reproductive health, empowerment and labour market
Life expectancy, schooling and GNI only
CO2 emissions, material footprint and sanitation
accepted.x: The GII measures gender inequality through reproductive health, empowerment and labour-market dimensions.
accepted.tq: Identify the three-domain composition and distinguish it from GDI and PHDI.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI adjusts HDI for:
accepted.x: PHDI, introduced in 2020, adjusts HDI for planetary pressures represented by carbon dioxide emissions and material footprint.
accepted.tq: Match the environmental adjustment with the index carrying the planetary-pressures label.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI

accepted.s:
Arrange the following indices in chronological order of their introduction in Human Development Reports:
A. GDI
B. Capability Poverty Measure
C. Human Poverty Index
D. IHDI

Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: GDI was introduced in 1995, CPM in 1996, HPI in 1997 and IHDI in 2010.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the 1996 and 1997 measures between them.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: GII — reproductive health, empowerment and labour market
PHDI — adjustment for CO2 emissions and material footprint
IHDI — ratio of female HDI to male HDI
accepted.x: The ratio of female to male HDI is the GDI. IHDI is HDI discounted for inequality.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped definition by distinguishing the closely related gender and inequality indices.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI

accepted.s: If there is no inequality in the distribution of human development, which relationship holds?
accepted.x: When there is no inequality, the inequality adjustment causes no loss, so HDI equals IHDI.
accepted.tq: Apply the meaning of the inequality adjustment to the limiting case of zero inequality.
accepted.sec: Related indices - HPI, CPM, IHDI, GDI, GII, PHDI
